sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: If you tuned in to Saturday Night Live, the weekend after last fall's election,
sentences.zh: 如果你在去年秋季大选后的那个周末收看了《周六夜现场》，

sentences.en: you may remember the sketch.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得那个小品。

sentences.en: A group of friends, all liberals, are gathered around their TV
sentences.zh: 一群自由派的朋友聚在电视机前，

sentences.en: as states begin to report voter tallies.
sentences.zh: 看着各州开始汇报投票统计结果。

sentences.en: It doesn't go the way they expect.
sentences.zh: 结果并不如他们所料。

sentences.en: All she has to do is come back and win Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 她只需要回来赢下威斯康星州，

sentences.en: come back and win Michigan, come back and win Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 赢下密歇根州，赢下宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: Some of the counties, the urban counties, they're so...
sentences.zh: 有些县，那些城市县，它们太……

sentences.en: Black people vote late!
sentences.zh: 黑人投票投得晚！

sentences.en: Making jokes about politics, politicians, and voters
sentences.zh: 拿政治、政客和选民开玩笑，

sentences.en: is a tradition as old as America itself.
sentences.zh: 是和美国本身一样古老的传统。

sentences.en: Cartoonists portrayed King George as a tyrant and a buffoon
sentences.zh: 漫画家们在独立战争期间，

sentences.en: during the Revolutionary War.
sentences.zh: 将乔治国王描绘成暴君和丑角。

sentences.en: More than a century ago, Mark Twain wrote that fleas
sentences.zh: 一个多世纪前，马克·吐温写道，跳蚤

sentences.en: can be taught nearly anything that a congressman can.
sentences.zh: 几乎能学会国会议员能学会的任何东西。

sentences.en: And in the 1960s, the Smothers Brothers used their TV platform
sentences.zh: 而在20世纪60年代，斯莫瑟斯兄弟利用他们的电视平台

sentences.en: to criticize the Vietnam War, much to the chagrin of network censors.
sentences.zh: 批评越战，这让电视网审查员非常恼火。

sentences.en: And if you ever get a war without blood and door, boy, I'll be the first to go.
sentences.zh: 如果你能打一场没有流血和死亡的战争，伙计，我第一个去。

sentences.en: But until then, Mr. McNamara...
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，麦克纳马拉先生……

sentences.en: These days, of course, comedians have a new target,
sentences.zh: 当然，如今喜剧演员们有了新的目标，

sentences.en: President Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统。

sentences.en: Today, we thought we'd talk with one of those comedians,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们想和其中一位喜剧演员聊聊，

sentences.en: the Iranian-American Maz Jobrani.
sentences.zh: 伊朗裔美国人马兹·乔布拉尼。

sentences.en: For him, the Trump administration ban on travelers from seven nations,
sentences.zh: 对他来说，特朗普政府对包括伊朗在内的七个国家实施的旅行禁令，

sentences.en: including Iran, has hit close to home.
sentences.zh: 让他感同身受。

sentences.en: Maz is a liberal and has strong feelings about President Trump,
sentences.zh: 马兹是一位自由派，对特朗普总统有着强烈的看法，

sentences.en: feelings that are increasingly showing up in a stand-up routine.
sentences.zh: 这些看法正越来越多地出现在他的单口喜剧表演中。

sentences.en: Listen, first of all, whether you like Trump or not,
sentences.zh: 听着，首先，不管你喜不喜欢特朗普，

sentences.en: you've got to admit, when he first started running,
sentences.zh: 你必须承认，当他刚开始竞选时，

sentences.en: everybody thought it was a joke.
sentences.zh: 所有人都以为这是个笑话。

sentences.en: Everybody was like, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在说，哈哈哈哈哈哈。

sentences.en: Now, no one can believe it.
sentences.zh: 现在，没人敢相信这是真的。

sentences.en: Everyone's like, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在说，哈哈哈哈哈哈哈哈。

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, finding the laughter in a moment of political strife.
sentences.zh: 今天在《隐藏的大脑》节目中，探讨在政治纷争时刻寻找笑声。

sentences.en: Maz Jobrani came to the United States when he was just a kid.
sentences.zh: 马兹·乔布拉尼还是个孩子时就来到了美国。

sentences.en: His family fled Iran during the 1979 revolution.
sentences.zh: 他的家人在1979年革命期间逃离了伊朗。

sentences.en: Over the years, Maz has made a name for himself with comedy that draws on parenting,
sentences.zh: 多年来，马兹凭借取材于育儿、

sentences.en: Persian culture, and politics.
sentences.zh: 波斯文化和政治的喜剧表演而声名鹊起。

sentences.en: He's the author of I'm Not a Terrorist, but I've played one on TV.
sentences.zh: 他是《我不是恐怖分子，但我曾在电视上扮演过》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He also has a new show out on CBS.
sentences.zh: 他还在哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）有一档新节目。

sentences.en: It's called Superior Donuts.
sentences.zh: 节目名叫《超级甜甜圈》。

sentences.en: Maz, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 马兹，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Maz, you know, I've always had the sense that comedians are really social scientists
sentences.zh: 马兹，你知道，我一直觉得喜剧演员其实是社会科学家，

sentences.en: because you can't do comedy unless you have a really sharp eye for human nature.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你对人性没有敏锐的洞察力，你就无法表演喜剧。

sentences.en: There's a joke that you did some months ago that reinforced this idea for me.
sentences.zh: 几个月前你讲的一个笑话让我更加坚信这一点。

sentences.en: It's about Donald Trump's attitude toward immigrants.
sentences.zh: 那是关于唐纳德·特朗普对待移民的态度。

sentences.en: Listen, the number one thing I've heard Trump supporters say, number one thing,
sentences.zh: 听着，我听到特朗普支持者说的第一件事，最主要的一件事就是，

sentences.en: I love him because he says what's on his mind.
sentences.zh: 我爱他，因为他有什么说什么。

sentences.en: He just says what's on his mind.
sentences.zh: 他就是有什么说什么。

sentences.en: He just says what's on his mind.
sentences.zh: 他就是有什么说什么。

sentences.en: You go, what are your thoughts on his policies?
sentences.zh: 你问，你对他政策的看法是什么？

sentences.en: I don't know about his policies.
sentences.zh: 我不了解他的政策。

sentences.en: He just says what's on his mind.
sentences.zh: 他就是有什么说什么。

sentences.en: I thought that was the dumbest thing I'd ever heard.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是我听过最蠢的话。

sentences.en: So I went to visit my mother, my own mother, Iranian lady.
sentences.zh: 所以我去探望我母亲，我自己的母亲，一位伊朗女士。

sentences.en: She had fallen for the line.
sentences.zh: 她也信了这套说辞。

sentences.en: My mom goes, Maz, I like this guy because he's saved what is on his mind.
sentences.zh: 我妈说，马兹，我喜欢这家伙，因为他有什么说什么。

sentences.en: I go, Mom, are you crazy?
sentences.zh: 我说，妈，你疯了吗？

sentences.en: He's anti-immigrant.
sentences.zh: 他是反移民的。

sentences.en: If he became president, your relatives couldn't come to visit you.
sentences.zh: 如果他当了总统，你的亲戚就不能来看你了。

sentences.en: She goes, I don't like them anyway.
sentences.zh: 她说，我本来就不喜欢他们。

sentences.en: So, Maz, you predicted what the Trump administration was going to do
sentences.zh: 那么，马兹，你在特朗普政府宣布针对伊朗旅客的禁令前几个月，

sentences.en: with travelers from Iran months before it was announced.
sentences.zh: 就预言了他们会这么做。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what's next in Donald Trump's playbook?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我唐纳德·特朗普的剧本里下一步是什么吗？

sentences.en: You know how hard it's been to write material?
sentences.zh: 你知道写段子有多难吗？

sentences.en: Because to do stand-up comedy, it takes time for the material to develop.
sentences.zh: 因为要表演单口喜剧，段子的打磨需要时间。

sentences.en: So you'll come up with a joke, you'll tweak it, you'll work it for six months,
sentences.zh: 所以你会想出一个笑话，进行调整，打磨六个月，

sentences.en: you'll really fine-tune it, and now you've got a good bit.
sentences.zh: 真正精雕细琢一番，现在你才算有了一个好的段子。

sentences.en: Well, with Trump, every day there's something new coming out.
sentences.zh: 而对于特朗普，每天都有新鲜事发生。

sentences.en: And then sometimes you do a joke that already feels dated.
sentences.zh: 有时你讲了一个笑话，却感觉已经过时了。

sentences.en: I did a joke last night about the travel ban, and it just felt dated to me already,
sentences.zh: 我昨晚讲了一个关于旅行禁令的笑话，但我觉得它已经过时了，

sentences.en: although you can continue to do it.
sentences.zh: 尽管你还可以继续讲。

sentences.en: So nobody knows what he's going to do next.
sentences.zh: 所以没人知道他下一步会做什么。

sentences.en: And I keep saying that Trump is good for comedy, but bad for the world.
sentences.zh: 我一直说特朗普对喜剧有好处，但对世界没好处。

sentences.en: What was the joke about the travel ban?
sentences.zh: 那个关于旅行禁令的笑话是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's just that I've been doing jokes about, I talk about how when the protests happened
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是我一直在讲关于……我谈到当旅行禁令在机场引发抗议时，

sentences.en: for the travel ban at the airport, I went down, I actually went down to the LAX and I protested.
sentences.zh: 我去了，我真的去了洛杉矶国际机场参加了抗议。

sentences.en: And one of the observations I said I made was that I realized quickly that white people born in America
sentences.zh: 我观察到的一点是，我很快意识到在美国出生的白人

sentences.en: protest differently than people of color or anyone who is an immigrant, because I'm an immigrant.
sentences.zh: 抗议的方式与有色人种或任何移民不同，因为我是移民。

sentences.en: And this actually happened, we were all protesting, but then when the cops came out in riot gear,
sentences.zh: 这事真的发生了，我们都在抗议，但当警察穿着防暴装备出来时，

sentences.en: I kind of felt like I wanted to go protest on the side, whereas all the white people just kept going at the cop.
sentences.zh: 我当时想退到一边抗议，而所有的白人却继续冲向警察。

sentences.en: And I was like, are you crazy?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，你们疯了吗？

sentences.en: But one guy, this actually happened, one guy had his finger in the face of the cop in riot gear.
sentences.zh: 但有一个人，这真的发生了，他把手指戳在防暴警察的脸上。

sentences.en: The cop had his baton, he was ready to go.
sentences.zh: 警察拿着警棍，准备动手了。

sentences.en: So this white guy had his finger in the face of the cop and just, I don't know what he was saying,
sentences.zh: 所以这个白人把手指戳在警察脸上，我不知道他在说什么，

sentences.en: but it looked like he was saying something along the lines of, this is my right and I'm going to protest or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但看起来他是在说类似“这是我的权利，我要抗议”之类的话。

sentences.en: And I got nervous for him and I got nervous for us.
sentences.zh: 我为他感到紧张，也为我们感到紧张。

sentences.en: I got nervous for everybody.
sentences.zh: 我为每个人感到紧张。

sentences.en: I can tell that you feel very strongly about Donald Trump and that there's much about this administration that upsets you.
sentences.zh: 我看得出你对唐纳德·特朗普有着强烈的看法，而且这届政府的很多做法让你感到不安。

sentences.en: But I'm also wondering what effect this has on your comedy.
sentences.zh: 但我也想知道这对你的喜剧有什么影响。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to be funny when you're angry at the same time, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你感到愤怒时，很难变得幽默，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I mean, some people have made a living doing that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，嗯，我的意思是，有些人就是靠这个为生的。

sentences.en: Louis Black, who's one of my favorite comedians, is angry and he's funny, very funny.
sentences.zh: 刘易斯·布莱克，我最喜欢的喜剧演员之一，他很愤怒，但他很幽默，非常幽默。

sentences.en: That's the last person on earth you want to give a firearm to.
sentences.zh: 那是地球上最后一个你想给他发枪的人。

sentences.en: Somebody teach in the fifth grade, are you me?
sentences.zh: 有人在教五年级，你是在说我吗？

sentences.en: You don't think at some point she's going to reach on her desk and go, shut up, you.
sentences.zh: 你不觉得在某个时刻她会伸手去拿桌上的东西说，闭嘴，你。

sentences.en: So there are those who have that personality.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有那种性格的人。

sentences.en: My personality is probably not as angry on stage.
sentences.zh: 我的性格在舞台上可能没那么愤怒。

sentences.en: So what I do is if I do get into a topic like that, I just make sure there's a punchline coming afterwards.
sentences.zh: 所以我做的是，如果我进入那样的话题，我会确保后面紧跟着一个包袱。

sentences.en: So I think you just got to keep in mind to have punchlines in there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你只需要记住在里面加入包袱。

sentences.en: I do have people, you know, I've been very active now on social media and I have people comment and say, stick to comedy.
sentences.zh: 确实有人，你知道，我现在在社交媒体上非常活跃，有人评论说，专注于喜剧吧。

sentences.en: You're a comedian, stick to comedy.
sentences.zh: 你是个喜剧演员，专注于喜剧吧。

sentences.en: And my response to those people is, then you should stick to accounting.
sentences.zh: 我对这些人的回应是，那你应该专注于会计工作。

sentences.en: Don't criticize my comedy.
sentences.zh: 别批评我的喜剧。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like we are, you are what you are.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就像我们是……你就是你。

sentences.en: I am a political human being.
sentences.zh: 我是一个有政治意识的人。

sentences.en: I have, that's one of my interests.
sentences.zh: 我有……那是我的兴趣之一。

sentences.en: I studied political science in college.
sentences.zh: 我在大学里学的是政治学。

sentences.en: I was actually going to get my PhD in poli-sci.
sentences.zh: 我本来打算去拿政治学博士学位。

sentences.en: And a lot of my material from early on in my career dealt with politics.
sentences.zh: 我职业生涯早期的很多素材都涉及政治。

sentences.en: So I've always considered myself as somebody who enjoys political humor.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直认为自己是一个喜欢政治幽默的人。

sentences.en: So I'm not going to stop.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会停止。

sentences.en: I know you spend time watching Fox News in the age of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在唐纳德·特朗普时代花时间看福克斯新闻。

sentences.en: And in some of your comedy, you talk about how this changes your own perception.
sentences.zh: 在你的一些喜剧中，你谈到了这如何改变了你自己的认知。

sentences.en: It's based on fear.
sentences.zh: 它是基于恐惧的。

sentences.en: It's all basically, like, I watch it from time to time to see what the other side is thinking a little bit.
sentences.zh: 基本上都是，就像，我时不时地看一看，看看另一方在想什么。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: I want to like, like, and then once you watch it a little bit, you start like doubting the people around you.
sentences.zh: 我想……然后一旦你看了一点，你就会开始怀疑周围的人。

sentences.en: I'm like, maybe my cousin Mahmoud is up to some s***.
sentences.zh: 我在想，也许我的表弟马哈茂德在搞什么鬼。

sentences.en: You're saying that you start to buy it?
sentences.zh: 你是说你开始相信了？

sentences.en: You know, it's very similar to what happened at the Republican National Convention.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这和共和党全国代表大会上发生的事情非常相似。

sentences.en: I mean, when they kept saying, make America great again, and you've got to make America safe, and America's in danger.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当他们一直说，让美国再次伟大，你必须让美国安全，美国处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And it's this, if you buy into that fear, I mean, they really were scaring people at that Republican National Convention to the point where you thought, oh, you know, if I'm there,
sentences.zh: 就是这样，如果你相信那种恐惧，我的意思是，他们在共和党全国代表大会上真的在吓唬人，以至于你会想，哦，你知道，如果我在那里，

sentences.en: I'm thinking I shouldn't go out in the streets because Muslims are coming to get me.
sentences.zh: 我在想我不应该走上街头，因为穆斯林要来抓我了。

sentences.en: And I think that if you watch those enough that you slowly start doubting and start, when you go into a subway store and there's a Muslim guy behind the counter, you start,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为如果你看多了这些，你就会慢慢开始怀疑，开始……当你走进一家地铁商店，柜台后面有一个穆斯林，你开始，

sentences.en: you know, doubting his intentions a little bit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，稍微怀疑他的意图。

sentences.en: How do you take that and turn that into comedy?
sentences.zh: 你如何把这些转化为喜剧？

sentences.en: How do you take stuff that's very serious, that people potentially care about, that people are potentially hurt by, how do you take that and turn that into a joke or a punchline?
sentences.zh: 你如何把非常严肃的事情，人们可能关心的事情，人们可能因此受到伤害的事情，转化为一个笑话或包袱？

sentences.en: Is there a method to doing it?
sentences.zh: 有什么方法吗？

sentences.en: I think sincere emotions and feelings about a subject, your sincere experiences with a subject.
sentences.zh: 我认为是对一个主题真诚的情感和感受，你对一个主题真诚的经历。

sentences.en: I talk about, for example, talking about the fear of ISIS, and I was doing a little bit about how I actually went to Turkey in November to do a show.
sentences.zh: 我谈论，例如，谈论对ISIS的恐惧，我讲了一点关于我十一月去土耳其演出时的事情。

sentences.en: And at 7 a.m.
sentences.zh: 早上7点，

sentences.en: one morning, somebody rang the door at the hotel room, and I was jet-lagged, and I got up, and I went and looked through the little peephole, and I look out,
sentences.zh: 有人敲酒店房间的门，我有时差，我起床，透过猫眼往外看，

sentences.en: and there was three Arab guys standing there in a triangular fashion, like one standing in the center, two flanking him.
sentences.zh: 有三个阿拉伯人以三角形的方式站着，一个站在中间，两个在两侧。

sentences.en: And I honestly, for a second, I thought, oh, my God, ISIS has come to get me.
sentences.zh: 我真的有一瞬间想，天哪，ISIS来抓我了。

sentences.en: And I just was scared, and I go, who is it?
sentences.zh: 我当时很害怕，我说，是谁？

sentences.en: And then the poor Arab guy, he kind of looked around, and he goes, Mustafa?
sentences.zh: 然后那个可怜的阿拉伯人环顾四周，说，穆斯塔法？

sentences.en: And I go, no, there's no Mustafa.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，没有穆斯塔法。

sentences.en: He goes, oh, oh, sorry, I thought Mustafa.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，哦，抱歉，我以为是穆斯塔法。

sentences.en: Mustafa, so they had come to the wrong door.
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法，所以他们敲错门了。

sentences.en: Just three Arab guys were, I guess, their buddy Mustafa must have been, you know, two doors down.
sentences.zh: 只是三个阿拉伯人，我想，他们的伙伴穆斯塔法一定在，你知道，两扇门之外。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But that's where, again, it became, when I was talking about it on stage, it was getting laughs because it was making fun of myself and how I had fallen for this fear.
sentences.zh: 但这就是，再次，它变成了，当我在舞台上谈论它时，它引起了笑声，因为它是在嘲笑我自己，以及我是如何陷入这种恐惧的。

sentences.en: So I think you take those situations, and you talk about the odds of you actually having something like this happen to you are low,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你利用这些情况，谈论你真正遇到这种事情的几率很低，

sentences.en: but how you can buy into it and how I bought into it.
sentences.zh: 但谈论你是如何相信它的，以及我是如何相信它的。

sentences.en: One of the things I find very interesting about your comedy from a psychological perspective, Maz,
sentences.zh: 从心理学的角度来看，我发现你的喜剧中有一点非常有趣，马兹，

sentences.en: is you talk about how being surrounded by stereotypes and profiling changes the way you think about yourself.
sentences.zh: 那就是你谈到了被刻板印象和侧写包围是如何改变你对自己看法的。

sentences.en: You did an interview some time ago with a public radio show, The World, and I want to play a short excerpt from it.
sentences.zh: 你之前在公共广播节目《世界》中接受过一次采访，我想播放其中的一小段。

sentences.en: This feeling I used to have after September 11th, I felt like whenever you passed through the metal detector, you just felt guilty.
sentences.zh: 那种我曾在9·11事件后产生的感觉，我觉得每当你通过金属探测器时，你就会感到内疚。

sentences.en: And I would go through it, and I would hear like, and I'd be like, I knew it.
sentences.zh: 我会走过去，然后我会听到，我会想，我早就知道了。

sentences.en: So that's a joke, of course,
sentences.zh: 当然，那只是个笑话，

sentences.en: but I understand this feeling of being suspicious of even yourself might have some parallels in real life as you've gone around the country to perform live shows.
sentences.zh: 但我理解这种甚至怀疑自己的感觉，在你全国各地进行现场表演时，可能在现实生活中也有一些相似之处。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, listen, we get bombarded with this stuff every day, every day, every day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听着，我们每天、每天、每天都被这些东西轰炸。

sentences.en: So it's going to be in our minds.
sentences.zh: 所以它会出现在我们的脑海里。

sentences.en: It's going to be there.
sentences.zh: 它会一直存在。

sentences.en: I mean, I did another bit in my special called I'm Not a Terrorist, but I've played one on TV.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在我的专场演出《我不是恐怖分子，但我曾在电视里演过一个》中还讲过另一个段子。

sentences.en: I do a joke about how I say I realized that I racially profile, and this actually happened again where I was on an airplane sitting towards the front,
sentences.zh: 我讲了一个笑话，说我意识到自己有种族偏见，这事儿确实又发生了一次，当时我在飞机上，坐在前排，

sentences.en: and before the door closed, this blonde girl, American girl, probably in her mid-20s, she came running to the front, seemed like she was having a panic attack,
sentences.zh: 在舱门关闭之前，有个金发女孩，美国女孩，大概20多岁，她跑向前面，看起来像是惊恐发作了，

sentences.en: and just was saying, I've got to get off this plane.
sentences.zh: 一直在说，我必须下飞机。

sentences.en: I can't do this.
sentences.zh: 我受不了了。

sentences.en: I can't fly.
sentences.zh: 我没法坐飞机。

sentences.en: And the stewardess came up and goes, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 空姐走过来问，怎么了？

sentences.en: We're about to leave.
sentences.zh: 我们马上就要起飞了。

sentences.en: And no, no, I can't.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我不行。

sentences.en: I've got to get off.
sentences.zh: 我必须下去。

sentences.en: And then the stewardess said, okay, let me ask the pilot.
sentences.zh: 然后空姐说，好吧，我去问问机长。

sentences.en: The pilot came out and said, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 机长出来说，好吧，没问题。

sentences.en: You can get off.
sentences.zh: 你可以下去。

sentences.en: So she just walked off.
sentences.zh: 于是她就走了下去。

sentences.en: And then we closed the door, and we took off.
sentences.zh: 然后我们关上舱门，起飞了。

sentences.en: And as we were taxiing, the passenger next to me looked at me and said, shouldn't we check to see if she had any luggage underneath?
sentences.zh: 就在滑行的时候，我旁边的乘客看着我说，我们不该检查一下她有没有行李在下面吗？

sentences.en: And my thought to the passenger was, no, she was just some 20-year-old white girl.
sentences.zh: 我对那位乘客的想法是，不，她只是个20岁的白人女孩。

sentences.en: Any baggage that she had was in her head.
sentences.zh: 她所有的行李都在她脑子里。

sentences.en: Whereas the honest truth is, again, this is how we all profile because of what we've seen.
sentences.zh: 而事实是，再说一次，这就是我们所有人因为所见所闻而进行归类的方式。

sentences.en: And I do this when I would do this in my stand-up.
sentences.zh: 我在单口喜剧表演中也会这样做。

sentences.en: I picked somebody out in the audience.
sentences.zh: 我从观众中挑了一个人。

sentences.en: There was an Egyptian, and I said, I guarantee you, I said, next time an airplane is about to take off,
sentences.zh: 有个埃及人，我说，我向你保证，我说，下次飞机快要起飞时，

sentences.en: go sit in the back of the plane you're in and just come running to the front.
sentences.zh: 坐到你所在飞机的后排，然后直接跑向前面。

sentences.en: And with your thickest Arabic accent, just say, I have to get off this plane right now.
sentences.zh: 用你最浓重的阿拉伯口音说，我现在必须下飞机。

sentences.en: I cannot do this.
sentences.zh: 我受不了了。

sentences.en: I have to get off this plane.
sentences.zh: 我必须下这架飞机。

sentences.en: And see if they let you off the plane.
sentences.zh: 看看他们会不会让你下飞机。

sentences.en: They will definitely stop the plane.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定会停下飞机。

sentences.en: They will search the plane.
sentences.zh: 他们会搜查飞机。

sentences.en: President Trump will give a speech that they thwarted a terrorist attack.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统会发表讲话，说他们挫败了一起恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: So what's that based on?
sentences.zh: 那么这是基于什么呢？

sentences.en: And that's based on these stereotypes that we've seen so many times over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这是基于我们一次又一次看到的这些刻板印象。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, I think we all stereotype.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我想我们所有人都会有刻板印象。

sentences.en: And that's not a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件好事。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to ask Maz about the psychology of crafting a joke and whether comedy can actually change our attitudes toward people from other cultures.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我要问问马兹关于创作笑话的心理学，以及喜剧是否真的能改变我们对其他文化人群的态度。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收看。

sentences.en: Maz, you've performed comedy all over the world, in the United States, the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 马兹，你在世界各地表演过喜剧，在美国，在中东。

sentences.en: Are there jokes that work here that don't work, for example, in Saudi Arabia?
sentences.zh: 有没有在这里行得通，但在沙特阿拉伯却行不通的笑话？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: I mean, that's, for the most part, a lot of material works, especially if you're doing material about your family everywhere you go.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在很大程度上，很多素材都是通用的，尤其是当你无论走到哪里都讲关于家庭的素材时。

sentences.en: When you do kid material, parents seem to sympathize.
sentences.zh: 当你讲孩子的内容时，父母们似乎会产生共鸣。

sentences.en: And I think we can all agree that kids can be the common enemy sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都能同意，孩子们有时会成为共同的敌人。

sentences.en: But there are jokes that sometimes don't work as well.
sentences.zh: 但有些笑话有时效果没那么好。

sentences.en: Well, I used to do a joke where I said, I said, having young kids, your time is not your own time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我以前讲过一个笑话，我说，有了小孩，你的时间就不是你自己的时间了。

sentences.en: You have to take care of your to-do list while they're napping.
sentences.zh: 你必须在他们午睡时处理你的待办事项。

sentences.en: You're almost like a Navy SEAL.
sentences.zh: 你简直就像个海豹突击队员。

sentences.en: You've got to be ready to go anytime, anyplace.
sentences.zh: 你必须随时随地准备出发。

sentences.en: I used to do a joke where I said, the other day, the kids were napping, and I went to my wife.
sentences.zh: 我以前讲过一个笑话，我说，那天孩子们在午睡，我去找我妻子。

sentences.en: I said, hey, the kids are napping.
sentences.zh: 我说，嘿，孩子们在午睡。

sentences.en: You know, let's make love.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们来亲热一下吧。

sentences.en: And my wife said, I'm not in the mood.
sentences.zh: 我妻子说，我没心情。

sentences.en: I said, well, I'm not in the mood either.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我也没心情。

sentences.en: But the kids are sleeping.
sentences.zh: 但孩子们在睡觉。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Move it.
sentences.zh: 快点。

sentences.en: Move it.
sentences.zh: 快点。

sentences.en: You know, we've got to kill bin Laden.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们得干掉本·拉登。

sentences.en: Let's do this.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: And then jokingly, I turned to the audience.
sentences.zh: 然后我开玩笑地转向观众。

sentences.en: I said, that's what we call sex in my house, killing bin Laden.
sentences.zh: 我说，这就是我们家所谓的性生活，干掉本·拉登。

sentences.en: And so that was the joke.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个笑话。

sentences.en: And in America, people appreciated it.
sentences.zh: 在美国，人们很欣赏它。

sentences.en: But then I was doing a show in Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 但后来我在沙特阿拉伯演出时。

sentences.en: And as you may know, the bin Laden family is a respected family in Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，本·拉登家族在沙特阿拉伯是一个受人尊敬的家族。

sentences.en: So I wasn't sure how they're going to respond.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道他们会作何反应。

sentences.en: And so I tried the joke.
sentences.zh: 于是我试了这个笑话。

sentences.en: And it kind of got a lukewarm response.
sentences.zh: 结果反响平平。

sentences.en: Like a nervous response.
sentences.zh: 就像一种紧张的反应。

sentences.en: Like a nervous response.
sentences.zh: 就像一种紧张的反应。

sentences.en: Like some people in the audience, like the younger guys in the audience were laughing.
sentences.zh: 就像观众中的一些人，比如年轻的观众在笑。

sentences.en: But the older, you know, families were not because I think they just felt it was disrespectful.
sentences.zh: 但年长的，你知道，家庭成员没有笑，因为我想他们觉得这很不尊重人。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's been times when some jokes don't go over as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，确实有几次笑话效果不佳。

sentences.en: But, you know, live and learn.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，活到老学到老。

sentences.en: So over the years, your comedy has often addressed Persian culture and tried to demystify that culture for other Americans.
sentences.zh: 多年来，你的喜剧经常涉及波斯文化，并试图为其他美国人揭开这种文化的神秘面纱。

sentences.en: This is a clip from your comedy special, I'm Not a Terrorist, but I've played one on TV.
sentences.zh: 这是你喜剧专场《我不是恐怖分子，但我曾在电视里演过一个》中的片段。

sentences.en: Persians, the Persians were very formal.
sentences.zh: 波斯人，波斯人非常正式。

sentences.zh: 我们是一种非常正式的文化。

sentences.en: I'll tell you how I realized how formal we are, okay?
sentences.zh: 我告诉你我是怎么意识到我们有多正式的，好吗？

sentences.zh: 这事儿最近才发生。

sentences.zh: 我在参加一个波斯人的活动。

sentences.en: And I was walking.
sentences.zh: 我正在走着。

sentences.en: And there was this Persian lady standing there.
sentences.zh: 那里站着一位波斯女士。

sentences.zh: 那个笑话的灵感来自哪里？

sentences.en: This actually happened.
sentences.zh: 这事儿真的发生了。

sentences.en: I was at an event, this Iranian fundraiser, and I stepped on this lady's toes.
sentences.zh: 我在参加一个活动，一个伊朗人的筹款活动，我踩到了一位女士的脚趾。

sentences.zh: 我没写那个笑话。

sentences.zh: 我真的只是踩到了她的脚趾。

sentences.en: And she literally said, no, please, don't worry.

sentences.en: It was my fault.
sentences.zh: 是我的错。

sentences.en: My foot was too long.
sentences.zh: 我的脚太长了。

sentences.en: She said that.

sentences.en: And that same night, I went on stage because it just wrote itself.
